reason: Ticket deliveries stall in delivery_pending when the landing into main fails; the worker needs the cause and the safe retry path, which no existing skill states. Born as the class "ticket landing and delivery failures" so later landing errors (conflicts, main moved, activation) patch into it.
The episode closed a ticket attempt blocked by an unset dispatch test command; the agent correctly asked the person rather than setting it, and the skill should say so.

The episode's agent merged and pushed a ticket branch by hand (ff-only into main, then push) after the delivery gate said the ticket stayed open pending merge. This skill already forbids by-hand merges, but its trigger ("landing fails or is stuck pending") never matched that situation, so the agent did not load it. The description now names the delivery wording and the temptation.
Adds the why behind the gate: a commit already on main does not satisfy the close check, so the agent's repeated manual landing cannot clear it. Stops the next agent from repeating the manual merge.

Same episode: after a manual push the map still reported "delivery: Ticket stays open. Missing: Merge this ticket's own commits into main, push, activate changed code, then clear its fault light." The skill's by-hand rule was correct but was stated as a warning, not as the observed consequence, so the worker treated a pushed commit as delivered.

A landing refused with "error: Entry 'src/metaform/modules/dispatch/README.md' not uptodate. Cannot merge." because the main checkout held another agent's uncommitted edits to files the ticket also changed. The skill had no entry for this refusal, so the worker had to rediscover the procedure; the trigger phrase should route it here.
Same episode: the correct handling was to leave the peer's edits alone and record the blocker, which the skill did not say. Without the rule a worker is tempted to clear the dirty files itself.

Rich decided (2026-10-21) that a landing never refuses for local edits: dirty checkouts are merged per file, and only a true clash is named for the owner. The title still says a landing refuses anything the checkout holds, which contradicts the new rule. Patched together with the body line that stated the old stop-and-wait behaviour.
The landing no longer uses read-tree (the kill-step test moved from 'read-tree' to 'checkout' in the same change). Naming the removed mechanism sends a future agent to a step that no longer runs.

Rich's rule (2026-10-21, closure-never-gated memory): dirty checkouts are merged per file, and an unasked refusal is a defect. The current body tells workers to stop and wait on any uncommitted edit, which now contradicts the code. The old rule stays only as the fallback for a checkout where the change is not on main.

Closure gating on the dispatch merges receipt was removed: op=done always closes, and feature commit/merge runs only when Full Auto is on, with no push, proof or restart gate. The skill still told agents a ticket stays open until the receipt exists, which now contradicts the rule.
The "Ticket stays open" reading is retired; closing is never gated on merge or push, so the skill must not tell agents the ticket is unfinished.
Ordinary landings never push and the ticket is closed by op=done, not by the landing; the receipt reported after a local merge is merged true, pushed false.

A landing reported conflicts in five files the branch had already merged from main, because merge_due used the recorded start as the three-way base. The fix (landing_base, merge-base when the branch merged main since its start) is the correct landing path and the skill should name it so agents stop hand-resolving.
